title: Ring Smart Lock el marşıyla şarj edilebilen ilk akıllı kilidini duyurdu
summary: Amazon'un sahibi olduğu Ring, pil bitme endişesini ortadan kaldıran çevrilebilir enerji koluna sahip ilk akıllı kilidini ve yeni 4K kamera serisini tanıttı.
body:
Ring Smart Lock, akıllı ev pazarında sıfırdan tasarlanan ve kullanıcıların pil bitmesi korkusuyla evde kilitli kalma endişesini ortadan hedefleyen ilk akıllı kilit sistemi olarak duyuruldu. Amazon'un akıllı ev markası Ring tarafından tanıtılan cihaz, kapı koluna entegre edilen özel bir enerji kolu sayesinde öne çıkıyor. Android Authority ve TechCrunch'ın aktardığına göre, cihazın pili tamamen bitse bile bu kolu birkaç kez çevirerek kilide anında güç vermek ve eve giriş yapmak mümkün oluyor.

## Farklı kontrol seçenekleri ve yeni kameralar

Standart tek silindirli sürgülü kilitlerin üzerine ek kablo gerektirmeden monte edilebilen Ring Smart Lock, parmak izi okuyucu, arkadan aydınlatmalı dokunmatik tuş takımı, Ring uygulaması ve Alexa komutları olmak üzere dört farklı erişim yöntemi sunuyor. Cihaz ayrıca akıllı ev ağlarını genişleten Amazon Sidewalk altyapısını da destekliyor. Ring ayrıca bu duyuruyla birlikte 4K kalitesinde görüntü sunan Outdoor Cam 4K Plus, Floodlight Cam 4K Plus, Spotlight Cam 4K Plus ve Indoor Cam 4K modellerinin yanı sıra bütçe dostu Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K kamerasını da görücüye çıkardı.

## Fiyat ve piyasaya çıkış tarihi

Teknoloji basınının aktardığı detaylara göre Ring Smart Lock, ABD'de 249 dolardan başlayan fiyatla satışa çıkacak; Türkiye fiyatı henüz açıklanmadı. Ürünün Amerika'da ilk çeyrekte raflardaki yerini alması beklenirken, yeni kameralardan bazıları bugünden itibaren satışa sunuldu.

**Neden önemli?** Akıllı kilit pazarında kullanıcıların en büyük çekincesi olan pil tükenmesi sorununa mekanik bir çözüm getiren el marşı mekanizması, geleneksel acil durum yöntemlerine pratik bir alternatif oluşturuyor.

source_texts.text:
Ring's upcoming smart lock addresses battery worries with a hand crank
Oct 7, 2026 — 10:00 AM ET
- Ring has announced its first-ever smart lock, which can be recharged with a built-in energy crank in the thumbturn.
- This smart lock includes a fingerprint scanner and a touchscreen keypad, and users can control it through the Ring app or Alexa commands.
- Ring has also launched four new indoor and outdoor 4K cameras, along with an entry-level 2K indoor pan-and-tilt camera.
Amazon-owned Ring sells a wide range of smart home products, including doorbells, cameras, security systems, and several other accessories. One product that’s missing from its portfolio is a smart door lock. The company is now filling that gap with its first-ever smart lock.
Known simply as the Ring Smart Lock, it practically eliminates battery-related anxiety, thanks to an “energy crank” built into the thumbturn. “Crank it a few times and the lock powers itself right back up,” Ring says in the announcement. It includes a fingerprint reader, a backlit touchscreen keypad, the Ring app, and Alexa commands, giving you several ways to control it.
The smart lock attaches to your door’s existing standard single-cylinder deadbolt and doesn’t need additional wiring, per the company. It works with Amazon Sidewalk, a crowdsourced mesh network created via nearby Amazon products. This basically means you won’t need to rely on your home Wi-Fi for functions like remote locking, with unlocks happening on the device itself.
Customers can also remotely grant access to friends or family, or set specific time slots when a particular person can enter. These controls and all additional functions are available via the Ring app. As you would imagine, it can connect with existing Ring doorbells, alarms, and cameras, and lets you manage actions through Alexa on Echo devices.
Even with its unique crank-based recharging system, the Ring Smart Lock is priced competitively at $249. The bad news, however, is that this product won’t be available until Q1 2027, and Ring hasn’t provided a specific date.
Also say hello to Ring’s new lineup of indoor and outdoor cameras
Ring has also released a new set of cameras, ranging from 4K indoor and outdoor units to a budget indoor camera.
First up is the Outdoor Cam 4K Plus, which offers a 140-degree view and will be available with a built-in battery, as well as hardwired, plug-in, and PoE options. Ring has set a $149.99 price tag for this outdoor camera.
Next, we’re looking at the Floodlight Cam 4K Plus and Spotlight Cam 4K Plus, priced at $219.99 and $199.99, respectively. The former offers 24/7 recording and smart detection features, but only in hardwired setups. Meanwhile, the outdoor spotlight camera offers a 140-degree view and a bright 550-lumen spotlight for deterrence. You can get it in solar, battery, and plug-in options.
Ring also announced the Indoor Cam 4K, the company’s first indoor camera with 4K, priced at $99.99. In addition to a 115-degree view, this camera supports dual-band Wi-Fi 6 and comes with a physical privacy shutter that instantly blocks the camera and microphone. All four cameras use Retinal Vision 4K, an imaging technology Ring showcased last year.
Lastly, Ring is launching the budget-friendly Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K today for $69.99. As the name suggests, it offers 2K video quality, plus 360-degree panning and 175-degree tilt, to follow subjects as they move. Like the Indoor Cam 4K, the Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K includes a privacy shutter to disable the camera and microphone.
The Indoor Cam 4K and the entry-level Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K will be available for purchase starting today, while the rest of the camera lineup will go on pre-order today. All cameras will be available in White and Black colorways.

source_texts.title: Ring’s first smart lock can be hand-cranked when its battery dies
source_texts.summary: Amazon-owned Ring is entering the smart lock market with a device designed to tackle a common concern: getting locked out when the battery dies
source_texts.text:
Ring, the Amazon-owned video doorbell maker, is entering a new market: smart locks.
Ring’s new device isn’t exactly a copy-and-paste of the other locks already on the market, however, as it tackles a big issue that often deters people from embracing this kind of smart home equipment: the fear of the battery dying and getting locked out.
To address this, Ring’s smart lock has added a power dial. If the battery on the device runs out, the homeowner can just turn the dial a few times to power the lock back up and enter their home.
Ring’s founder Jamie Siminoff said the idea to rethink smart locks came to him when he was looking to buy a lock for a vacation home. “I struggled because this particular house will get used very little, and I know the freaking battery will die on it,” he said.
He also worried that family or friends visiting the house might get stuck outside, as the door isn’t connected to a power source, and any smart lock would be dependent on the battery.
“I’m like, well, why don’t we just fix this,” he said. Using AI, he started working on a project to create a lock you could hand-crank just enough to power the lock to open. Once you’re in, you could then take out the rechargeable battery pack and charge it as usual.
Siminoff says the battery on Ring’s new lock will last about a year, and will alert users when it’s time to charge via the Ring app. The app also allows users to configure access for people who may need periodic access, like dog walkers or house cleaners. Eventually, the company wants to allow third-party app makers to design specialized software for the lock so it can be used in other ways — for example, Airbnb owners who may need to regularly change codes.
The Ring lock also offers four different ways to get in, so you won’t have to worry about forgetting a code. You can either use the device’s fingerprint reader, a backlit touchscreen keypad, the Ring app, or Alexa.
Siminoff admitted that the lock may be comparable to others on the market, but he thinks the fact that it addresses the anxiety over being locked out will be its biggest selling point.
“I do think the power thing is a huge limiter of why people are not buying, and why they’re not putting them in, and why they’re worried about them,” he said.
It’s also true that when smart locks do offer some sort of backup method, they usually involve something cumbersome and less secure — like hiding a physical key somewhere on the property.
Ring’s smart lock will fit a standard single-cylinder deadbolt, and will be available to purchase in the U.S. in the first quarter of 2027, after it receives FCC authorization. It will come in three finishes: black, silver, or brass.
Alongside the lock, Ring also introduced four new 4K cameras: the Outdoor Cam 4K Plus, Spotlight Cam 4K Plus, Floodlight Cam 4K Plus, and a pan-tilt Indoor Cam 4K.
